title: Screencast timeline (edit-decision list) v2
description: One take's observer/actor clips and edit events, written by screencast.timeline.Timeline (a Robot Framework ListenerV3) from real keyword start/end times. The composer (screencast.compose) reads this file, and only this file, to build the picture-in-picture output; the verifier (screencast.verify) reads it to know what to expect. All paths are relative to the take directory (var/screencasts/<story>/<take>/).

version.description: The composer and verifier refuse any other value.

observer.description: The single recording that spans the whole take -- opened first and closed last -- that every actor turn is composited against.

actors.description: One entry per recorded actor turn, in chronological order.

tracks.description: Optional: extra contexts recorded for the whole take alongside the observer (Screencast.start_track()/end_track()), each independently focusable as the composer's main view via Focus(view=<name>) -- unlike compose()'s external tracks= (a secondary recording the engine itself never captured), always an always-present corner inset. Absent on a timeline written before this field existed.

video.description: Path to the recorded .webm, relative to the take directory.

actor.description: Persona name, matching the 'actor' field on this clip's turn_start/turn_end events.

video.description: Path to the recorded .webm, relative to the take directory.

offset.description: Seconds from the observer recording's start to this clip's start (context creation), measured with the same clock as the observer, i.e. time.monotonic() - started.

duration.description: Optional: the clip's measured duration in seconds (ffprobe). The composer re-measures this itself and does not trust a stale value here.

name.description: Matches a focus event's 'view' to make this track the main view -- see Focus(view=name).

video.description: Path to the recorded .webm, relative to the take directory.

offset.description: Seconds from the observer recording's start to this track's start (context creation), measured with the same clock as the observer, i.e. time.monotonic() - started. Unlike an actor clip's offset, not constrained to be non-negative in principle, but start_track() always measures it against an already-running observer clock, so it never is in practice.

focusable.description: Whether Focus(view=name) may make this track the composer's main view at all. Omitted (true) is the original behaviour. false is a structural guarantee that this track is always a corner inset and never main -- e.g. a terminal a story wants visible but never full-frame -- so a later edit of the story (or the timeline itself) cannot accidentally promote it by naming it in a focus event; the composer falls back to ordinary actor/observer resolution the same way it already does for an unknown track name.

corner.description: Which corner this track's own always-present inset is pinned to. Defaults to bottom-left, the original (and only, before this field existed) behaviour -- same corner names compose()'s external tracks=/--track already accepts. Set it to avoid a collision when two or more tracks (or a track and a focus-demoted actor/observer inset) would otherwise land in the same corner at once.

fade.description: Whether this track's own corner inset fades out: its left third stays fully opaque and the remaining two-thirds fade to transparent on a logarithmic curve, letting the main view show through behind it. Independent of 'focusable' -- a track can fade while still being eligible to become main (the fade only ever applies to its inset rendering, never to a segment where it is main and rendered full-frame).

scale.description: This track's own inset scale, as a fraction of the main frame's width -- only ever affects its inset rendering, same as a focus event's own 'scale' affects the actor/observer inset (never a segment where this track is main and rendered full-frame, which always fills the whole frame regardless).

margin.description: This track's own inset margin from its corner, in pixels.

border.description: This track's own inset border width, in pixels.

view.description: Which recording is the main (full-frame) view from this point on; the others become insets. 'actor' and 'observer' are always recognized; any other value names a track opened with start_track() (see the top-level 'tracks' field) -- the composer falls back to 'observer' if it names a track that was not recorded or is not yet available at this point in the take.

scale.description: Inset scale, as a fraction of the main frame's width.

solo.description: true renders only 'view', full-frame, with no inset of any kind from this point on -- not the usual actor/observer cross-inset, and not any track's own always-present corner inset either. Stays in effect until the next focus event says otherwise. There is no other way to turn an inset back off once a turn or a track has made one available -- see compose._view_at's own docstring.

duration.description: Extra seconds to hold the observer's frame at 'time' before continuing. Must not be negative once the overlap tolerance (screencast.timeline.OVERLAP_TOLERANCE) is applied.

recorded.description: True for a hold the library itself derived from real elapsed recording time (e.g. the return-to-observer wait after a turn), as opposed to a story's own Hold call. The composer does not insert a synthetic freeze for one (that time is already real footage in the observer clip); the verifier's dead_air check does not count it as a wait.

duration.description: Seconds the story spent waiting -- for a task to appear, a mail to arrive, a fixed Sleep -- during which nothing was being driven on screen. Recorded by the library's listener around the outermost waiting keyword (Sleep, Wait Until Keyword Succeeds, the engine's own waits, or any keyword tagged 'screencast:wait'); waits shorter than screencast.library.WAIT_MIN_RECORDED are not recorded. The composer ignores these events; the verifier's dead_air check judges them.

keyword.description: The waiting keyword's name, for the finding's message.

duration.description: How long the cue stays on screen, in seconds. The composer maps 'time' (raw, observer-clock) to the cue's position in the composed output -- adding every inserted chapter/hold segment at or before it -- but does not otherwise adjust 'duration'.
